newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RUGBY UNION-BRAIN'S LATE TRY SEALS CHIEFS' WIN.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-BRAIN'S LATE TRY SEALS CHIEFS' WIN.

text.p: Waikato Chiefs' number eight Errol Brain scored a try with less than two minutes left to seal a 33-26 win against New South Wales in the Super 12 competition on Saturday.
The late try broke the deadlock at the Sydney Football Stadium after New South Wales levelled the scores with a spirited second-half comeback.
Test centre Frank Bunce set up the clinching try with a clever change of direction to confound the New South Wales defence.
The New Zealanders dominated the early stages with two tries from All Black winger Eric Rush that gave the visitors a 17-9 lead at halftime.
Rush exploited gaps in the New South Wales defence to twice cross the line uncontested. Waikato captain and forward Ian Jones created both opportunities by winning fine line-out possession.
Fullback Matthew Cooper converted all three tries and kicked four penalties.
Australia test fullback Matthew Burke scored the bulk of his side's points with one try, two conversions and three penalties. Prop Richard Harry barged over for the other try.
New South Wales suffered a further blow when Italy test second rower Mark Giacheri sustained a suspected knee ligament injury and was forced to leave the field after 25 minutes.
Team officials said the injury could sideline Giacheri, who was making his debut for New South Wales, for the rest of the Super 12 competition.
But there was better news for Australia test captain and front row forward Phil Kearns, who played the final 15 minutes after being out for 18 months because of injury.
